title: Factor-remainder theorem bridge to univariate algebraic closure

problemStatement.formal: (X-C(a))\mid p \Longleftrightarrow p(a)=0,\quad p \bmod (X-C(a))=C(p(a)),\quad \operatorname{IsAlgClosed}(k)\Rightarrow \forall f\ne 0,\ 0<\deg f\Rightarrow \exists a, f(a)=0.
problemStatement.plain: Record the Lean-supported polynomial root/divisibility bridge behind elementary factorization and one-variable algebraic-geometry reductions. The current files prove the factor theorem, the remainder theorem, and a univariate weak Nullstellensatz consequence over algebraically closed fields.
whyMatters: The factor theorem is the algebraic hinge between roots and linear factors.
The remainder theorem gives an executable evaluation shortcut for polynomial division by a linear term.
The univariate Nullstellensatz bridge shows how these elementary facts scale into algebraic-closure arguments.

proven: `factor_theorem` proves `(X - C a) | p` if and only if `p.eval a = 0`.
`remainder_theorem` proves that reduction modulo `X - C a` leaves the constant polynomial `C (p.eval a)`.
`weak_nullstellensatz_univariate` proves that every nonzero nonconstant polynomial over an algebraically closed field has a root.
open: A full Berlekamp-Zassenhaus or Hensel-lifting formalization is not part of the current Lean inventory and should remain a follow-on target.
knownResults.goal: Use the completed factor/remainder statements as the safe foundation for later polynomial-factorization metadata and proof work.
